angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 431,334 km at 148.38 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.7396 +/- 0.0197 mas (same row, RUWE 0.97): 148.38 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.62 +/- 0.02 solar radii from Adams et al. 2021, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-156 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021PSJ.....2..152A/abstract): 431,334 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.642263 +/- 0.022039 solar masses from Mayo et al. 2018, the stellar mass of K2-156 b's parameter set from Mayo et al. 2018 (the default leaves it empty) in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....155..136M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4460 +/- 50 K from Adams et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-156 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021PSJ.....2..152A/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Adams et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-156 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021PSJ.....2..152A/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-156.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.661, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
